cohorts.subjects: Living adults whose T2-weighted lower lumbar (L3-S1) MRI was retrieved from the digital archive of the University Hospital of the University of Utah, Salt Lake City, USA, and anonymized; scans picked because the radiology diagnosis named no specific low back disorder, the clinical reason for each scan unknown to the authors. Inclusion: aged 20 to 40. Subjects excluded for evidence of morphological alteration of the lumbar or thoracic spine (crushed vertebral body, trauma) or known pathology likely to alter geometry (scoliosis, tumour); no count given. Per structure only: Pfirrmann grade V discs excluded (9 male discs: 2 L3/L4, 4 L4/L5, 3 L5/S1) and the L5/S1 end-plates of 23 subjects (13 F, 10 M) whose oblique slices were missing; the subject's other structures kept. Country USA; ethnicity not reported. IRB approval at Auburn University and the University of Utah. The rows quoted as Tang [31] in Tables 5 to 7 print this cohort's Table 4 means and SDs and its 55 F / 52 M (Inference: ref. 31 is the first author's 2013 dissertation on the same data set), so they repeat Table 4 and are not a separate sample.

techniques.instrument: Siemens MAGNETOM Avanto 1.5 T, subjects head-first supine; sagittal and transverse T2-weighted scans, TR 3000-4770 ms, TE 80-110 ms, slice thickness 3-4.5 mm; OsiriX 4.1.1 (32-bit) on a workstation; pixel size, matrix and field of view not stated
techniques.how: On transverse slices, taken only in oblique slices to limit distortion (Inference: slices angled parallel to each disc), each disc (IVD) and the end-plate cranial (CrEP) and caudal (CaEP) to it were traced by hand. CSA is the area inside the traced periphery; APD the distance between the anterior-most and posterior-most points of the contour (Fig. 1: the bounding rectangle's AP side, which for a kidney-shaped section reaches the posterolateral lobes); FD the distance between the right and left lateral-most points; MSD the distance between the mid-sagittal extents (the midline chord, ending in the posterior notch of a kidney-shaped section). The CrEP of disc Lx/Ly is the inferior end-plate of Lx and the CaEP the superior end-plate of Ly (the reading's levels follow this). How levels were counted, and whether transitional vertebrae were looked for, is not stated.
techniques.observers: the published values are observer I's first round; two observers measured 40 scans twice, a month apart in random order, for reliability only: ICC(3,1) 0.906 to 0.996 and Pearson 0.904 to 0.997 (Table 3)

techniques.instrument: computed from the MRI diameters of mri_t2_oblique_transverse
techniques.how: Ellipse-approximated area, formula (1) APD x FD x pi/4 (attributed to Panjabi [27]) and formula (2) MSD x FD x pi/4 (attributed to Hutton and Adams [39]), each compared with the traced CSA by level; the reading holds only the percentage errors the Results print.

within_paper: One pool: the 109 Utah subjects (utah_mri) give every disc and both end-plates of each level from the same scans, so the IVD, CrEP and CaEP rows of a level are of the same people, and the L3/L4, L4/L5 and L5/S1 rows overlap almost wholly (all 55 women at every level; men 52, 50 and 51 after grade V discs; L5/S1 end-plates 42 F and 41 M after the 23 missing slices), p. 4117 (PDF 2), Tables 2 and 4 pp. 4119-4120 (PDF 4-5). Table 2's three level samples are subsets of the same 109, its female rows identical across levels. The reliability set (40 scans, 20 F and 20 M) is drawn from the same scans and measured by two observers twice; the published values are observer I's first round, so Table 3 is of the same specimens as part of Table 4, p. 4118 (PDF 3). The Tang [31] rows of Tables 5-7 repeat this cohort's Table 4 (Inference from equal values); every other quoted study is a separate cohort, and the two Postacchini groups (Italian, Indian) and the two Turk and Celan rows are separate subjects. No value of the paper's own is pooled with a quoted one.
